workflows.description: Canonical reusable workflow for grounded retrieval of information of a requested kind about a resolved entity, especially authenticated self-relative questions about papers, affiliations, roles, and predicate-filtered extents.
workflows.content: Resolve the target entity from authenticated or explicit context, identify the requested information kind, prefer predicate-incidence and relation retrieval before broad inventory or lexical search, filter retrieved results by the requested type or extent, and answer directly from grounded represented evidence.

input_mappings.description: Pass through the user's entity-information request.

llm_policy.response_contract_text: Answer the user directly from grounded represented evidence. For broad self-profile, represented-self, authorship, ownership, affiliation, role, and other entity-relative relation questions, first fetch the focal entity concept, inspect predicate incidence with argument type counts, retrieve narrowed relation evidence, and check uncertainty-bearing relationship assertions for the same focal entity. When the user asks to separate established facts from likely inferences, report asserted relation/focal-concept evidence separately from uncertain or proposed relationship assertions; do not merge those categories. For papers, inspect predicate incidence before relation paging, then filter the resulting extent by the requested type before answering. If predicate incidence for a paper request exposes #V#author_of or #V#owner_of with paper-like type counts or sample groundings, the next relation lookup must use find_relations_with_argument with a predicate_filter containing those exact predicate IDs; do not use an unfiltered relation page first. If predicate incidence exposes role-expansion summaries for reified/event/claim neighbours, use role-filler type counts to choose the follow-up extent and do not treat the reified neighbour itself as the answer entity. Do not claim that no matching results exist unless the relation-bearing and uncertainty-bearing evidence in this turn supports that negative conclusion. If grounded evidence is insufficient, say that clearly instead of guessing. When using relation hits, map the returned related concept by argument direction: if the call used `argument_index` `subject`, use `target_concept_id`; if `object`, use `source_concept_id`. Emit every relation-grounded result as a Markdown bullet with a resolved `#V#...` concept ID wherever that relation-hit concept ID is available. Never emit relation-grounded results as bare assertion syntax such as `subject --predicate--> object`. If a related concept ID is missing, do not fabricate one: omit that item from the list and state clearly that no usable `#V#` ID was returned. Use a single-item bullet if only one grounded entity is returned. Relation-grounded outputs must be bullet entries with the resolved `#V#` ID token for navigation.
